scope: Root-cause diagnosis of intermittent store-link listing loads; production code and schema unchanged.

confirmed.cause: Authorization-scoped metadata aggregation reads non-covering indexes
Global metadata lock covers SQL; waiting callers have already borrowed MySQL connections
confirmed.evidence: Web connection pool limit 6; 2026-10-06 17:35:29, 31, 32, 33 repeated 10-second acquire timeouts. A slow scope blocks cached scopes too. Today 12:22, seven /api/store-links failures occurred in pre-request user permission lookup while acquiring a pooled connection, before the listing query started.

confirmed.cause: Synchronization status refresh duplicates and aborts initial list requests; overlapping status requests leave duplicate polling timers
DBUtils retries query-timeout OperationalError 3024 twice while holding the logical pooled connection
confirmed.evidence: Offline fake-driver assertion verifies 3 executions for one execute call. Production Mercado product-list COUNT stages recorded approximately 24.2 seconds against MAX_EXECUTION_TIME(8000); same Web pool reported 10-second acquisition timeouts.

validation.read_only_scoped_queries: Each query bounded at 15 seconds; all-store three slow queries reached limit. No schema changes.

frontend_reproduction.method: Real function source executed in a Node VM with mocked DOM, fetch, and timers; zero API access

results.scenario: Open store-links while the background sync is running
The store-links tab is inactive when the sync status responds
Two activations overlap before either sync status request returns

validation.dbutils_retry: Offline fake-driver assertions passed; no network or database access.

fix_priorities: Perform SQL outside the global cache lock, coordinate per scope, and check cached metadata before borrowing a MySQL connection.
Avoid duplicate automatic list refreshes and duplicate status polling.
Restrict DBUtils retries to actual connection failures; SQL execution timeouts must not execute three times. Optimize scoped product-list counts that contend for the same Web pool.
limits: Timing samples represent local SQL execution, not complete browser/network load times. Listing measurements omit workflow marker decoration.
Workflow SQLite sample was fast; no evidence it is the main bottleneck.
No production application patch, index creation or service restart performed.
